chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Regarding the slave man who has a free woman as his wife, he (peace be upon him) said: 'His children are free. So if the slave is emancipated, he joins his father (in terms of lineage/status).'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of children born to a slave father and a free mother in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of 'tahrir' (emancipation) extending to the family unit, ensuring that children born to a slave father and free mother are born free, a ruling distinct from some Sunni schools that may apply 'um al-walad' logic differently. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the father's eventual manumotion does not alter the children's pre-existing free status but rather completes the household's legal unity. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on social mobility and the dignity of the 'ummah' within the domestic sphere.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding the slave who happens to have the free woman under him (as a wife). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘His children would be free. So if the slave is emancipated, it would be attached with its father’.
